title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction: The page continues the previous one. There Grothendieck notes that the functor Ind(finitely generated fields) -> fields is an equivalence. It follows that the three invariants he attaches to a field can be recovered from their restrictions to finitely generated fields. These invariants are: B_K, the classifying topos of the absolute Galois group, i.e. the étale topos of Spec K; Pi_K, the profinite fundamental groupoid of Spec K, whose objects are the separable closures; and E_{Kbar/K} (also written Gamma_{Kbar K}), the Galois group of a chosen separable closure. These restricted functors keep 'all the fidelity properties' of the original ones on absolutely finitely generated fields. The fidelity properties meant here are the expected full faithfulness of K |-> Pi_K up to inner automorphisms, i.e. birational anabelian geometry. Grothendieck says he will mostly restrict to such fields from now on. He also warns that a purely algebraic description of the profinite (fundamental) pro-groups attached to fields that are not finitely generated will be needed. His example is C, 'more precisely (C, Cbar)!'. The exclamation is ironic: C is algebraically closed, so Cbar = C, and its Galois group is trivial. C matters because it is the base for comparison with transcendental fundamental groups. The dominant role is given to the prime field Q, hence to B_Q and Pi_Q. Pi_Q has a canonical object, Qbar_0, the algebraic closure of Q inside C. He defines (5) Gamma_Q = E_{Qbar_0/Q}, and allows Gamma_{Qbar/Q} for any algebraic closure. For every field K of characteristic 0 he then starts to introduce the structural morphisms B_K -> B_Q and Pi_K -> Pi_Q. On the next page these become, after choosing a base point Kbar, a homomorphism E_{Kbar/K} -> Gamma_{Qbar/Q} given by restriction to the algebraic closure of Q in Kbar. Its kernel, the 'geometric part' Gal(Kbar/K·Qbar), and the image, an open subgroup Gal(Qbar/Qbar∩K), give the standard geometric/arithmetic exact sequence. The purpose is to set up the framework of 'La Longue Marche': Galois groups of finitely generated fields over Q, viewed as objects over Gamma_Q, as the arena for anabelian questions.
errors: No mathematical error on this page. The remark about (C, Cbar) is a deliberate joke (C is algebraically closed), not a mistake.

The neighbouring page's claim that the projective-limit formulas (1) are 'not true' is debatable. For Galois groups, restriction gives an isomorphism Gal(Kbar/K) ≅ lim Gal(Kbar_i/K_i). Étale topoi of limits of affine schemes are limits of topoi (SGA 4 VII). This page argues via the Ind-equivalence instead, so the reading of 'n'est pas vraie' there may be a transcription issue.

ideas.what: Invariants B_K, Pi_K, E_{Kbar/K} of a field are determined by their restriction to absolutely finitely generated fields, via Ind(f.g. fields) ≃ fields
ideas.modern_name: Extension of functors along the Ind-completion; continuity of étale topoi and Galois groups

deep.surprise_reason: This is foundational set-up material for La Longue Marche: the Galois topos/groupoid/group of a field, reduction to finitely generated fields, and Gamma_Q as base. All of it is standard and present in Grothendieck's circulated texts (Longue Marche, letter to Faltings, Esquisse). The only flavour is the ironic remark on (C, Cbar).
transcription_corrections: Line 1: the struck word after 'idoines,' is a deleted fragment ('vu'/'vxx'); the meaning is 'des corps vers les gadgets idoines, avec toutes les propriétés de fidélité'.
'des pro-groupes fon[damentaux]' is uncertain. The image looks more like 'des pro-groupes-groupoïdes' or 'pro-groupes profinis'. The preceding 'K...' begins a phrase such as 'K... algébriques'.
'associé p.ex. : C (plus précisément, : (C, C̄)!)' should read 'associé p.ex. à C (plus précisément, à (C, C̄) !)'.
'Q, dans [?]' should probably read 'Q, donc par B_Q et Π_Q'.
Formula (5): the symbol is Γ_Q (with a doubled stroke), = E_{Q̄_0/Q}.
Final line: 'pour les corps K de type fini sur Q, on a ...' (sentence continued on next page).
